headline: Highest risk is medium: MinerU’s MCP/API surfaces can create prompt-injection and cascading-error pathways, while the pair otherwise lacks shared write access or direct data overlap.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: MinerU exposes an MCP Server and API surfaces, while the awesome-list agent is non-runnable and has no I/O surfaces. There is no documented direct bridge, but if MinerU ingests attacker-controlled documents and forwards content through MCP, prompt-like content could reach downstream consumers. Uncertainty about the exact orchestration pushes this above low.
conditions: IF MinerU is connected to another agent through MCP or API output parsing
IF attacker-controlled document text is treated as instructions by the downstream consumer
mitigations: Disable MCP exposure for the MinerU session
Route MinerU output through a strict schema validator
Strip instruction-like text from extracted documents before forwarding
Use a human review step before any downstream action
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to all extracted fields

B_data_leakage.rationale: Profile A touches no data classes and is non-runnable; Profile B processes documents locally and is marked private/offline, with allowlisted egress only. No shared workspace or secrets are documented, so a leakage pathway is not evident. The remaining risk is limited to accidental forwarding of extracted document text if an operator bridges outputs manually.
conditions: IF extracted document text is manually copied into another system
IF MinerU is configured to send outputs to an external API endpoint
mitigations: Keep MinerU offline except for allowlisted destinations
Do not place sensitive documents in shared folders
Review output before exporting it
Separate operator accounts for each agent
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent workspace isolation

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Agent A has no write or execution surfaces and is non-runnable, while Agent B cannot write files, modify git state, or spawn subprocesses. Overlapping mutable-resource writes are therefore absent in the profiles, making capability conflict unlikely. The only shared surface is read/processing of documents, which does not create a write race.
conditions: IF a separate orchestrator grants both agents write access to the same directory
IF an external wrapper adds shared mutable state not shown in the profiles
mitigations: Keep both agents read-only in the same run
Avoid shared git or filesystem targets
Run MinerU in a separate workspace
Verify no wrapper adds write permissions
requires-engineering: add locking if shared state is introduced

D_cascading_error.rationale: MinerU produces extracted text, tables, and OCR output that a downstream system could treat as authoritative, while the awesome-list agent provides no verification or action-taking role. If MinerU output is forwarded into another workflow without checks, extraction errors can cascade into incorrect decisions or documents. The interaction is inferred rather than directly documented, so uncertainty keeps this at medium.
conditions: IF MinerU output is used as authoritative input to another workflow
IF no verification step checks OCR or table extraction before reuse
mitigations: Require human verification of extracted fields
Compare OCR output against source documents for critical records
Mark MinerU output as untrusted by default
Use confidence thresholds before downstream use
requires-engineering: add automated cross-checks against source files

E_compliance.rationale: No regulated data class is documented for agent A, and agent B’s profile does not indicate PHI, EU PII, or residency-sensitive handling. With no stated compliance mismatch, there is no provable residency or certification conflict in this pair. The other agent is not cited separately because the risk is absent rather than merely unobserved.
conditions: IF regulated data classes such as PHI or EU PII are introduced into the workflow
IF a deployment policy imposes residency or retention constraints not shown here
mitigations: Classify inputs before processing
Block regulated data until compliance review
Document retention and deletion settings
Restrict exports to approved destinations
requires-engineering: add residency-aware routing
